question: Can tenant B infer the cache state of A's known, identical target request without knowing its exact arrival time, while A/B have stable disjoint salts?
model: Local Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, vLLM 0.17.1, C0 (max_num_batched_tokens 256, long_prefill_token_threshold 64), RTX 3090, prefix caching on, complete 16-token answers, direct B release through diagnostic-stripping proxy
fixed_salts: One random 256-bit salt for A and one different random 256-bit salt for B, stored in salts.json and reused across all 24 fresh backend starts. B does not receive A's salt; the measurement client holds both solely to simulate the two roles.
prompts: Unmodified 548-token Qwen document prompts from data/document-workload-20261103/prompts.json. A target is exactly document A in warm and cold; B always sends documents A-D. No Case NNN or other per-condition text changes. One fresh backend per case prevents prior trial cache state from contaminating the next with the fixed salts.
conditions: Before the measured group, A completes one 1-token request: A for warm, D for cold. After 250 ms quiet, A's 16-token target is A in both. Controls: absent has D preparation but no target; other_cold has A preparation and a cold D target. All preparations and targets of a given kind have equal token/output counts.
timing: B's four requests start at intended offsets 0/10/20/30 ms in one shuffled order. A's target starts at a hidden offset chosen before measurement from 0/150/300/450 ms, with two matched warm/cold pairs per offset. Same offset and B order within each pair. Warm/cold order randomized within pair; four warm-first and four cold-first pairs. Four A-absent and four other-cold controls interleaved, one after each pair. B knows the offset range/distribution but not the realized value or A's timestamps.
plan: cases.json, seed 202611032901. Eight matched warm/cold pairs, 16 primary cases, plus 8 controls; 24 fresh backend starts, randomized pair sequence. No automatic expansion.
attacker: Freeze the earlier direct-release T1/T2/R2/RT StandardScaler + LogisticRegression(C=1) models by fitting only on results/tenant-scheduler-20261103/dev/trials.jsonl (8 warm and 8 cold, 548-token prompts, known 15-ms offset), then apply without refitting or threshold changes. Features use only B's own send order, IDs and complete send/receive times. Primary: held-out T1 accuracy and development-selected-direction T1 AUC plus matched warm/cold sign across 8 pairs. T2/R2 secondary.
decision: A promising desynchronized result requires exact prompt and fixed-salt cache integrity, no B hits, all 8 victim intervals overlapping at least one B request in each condition, and at least 7/8 paired T1 differences in the prior warm-earlier direction or T1 AUC >=0.75 with at least 12/16 classifier hits. If signal is absent, report the narrower synchronized boundary; do not tune offsets or model. Controls assess whether B detects generic A work or A presence rather than document-specific cache state.
limits: B is still told that A may start within a 450-ms window; all positive target intervals are engineered to overlap B's requests. Fresh engine per case is a controlled research design, not a production traffic pattern. One model, GPU, loopback, no outside load, one target document and output length.
